What to do with IPv6 traffic of other apps while the VPN is on.
IPv6 goes nowhere, apps fall back to IPv4. Nothing leaks past the VPN. Recommended.
IPv6 is sent through the proxy. Needs a server with IPv6 access; sing-box and Xray only.
Fingerprint, face or screen PIN when opening Hydra and after 30 s in the background. Screenshots of the app are blocked.
Needs Android 9+ and a screen lock (PIN, pattern or fingerprint) set up on the device.
The VPN keeps working. Unlock to see servers and settings.
UUIDs, passwords, Reality keys and subscription tokens are shown as dots. Copy, QR and Share still use the full link.
Now: Always-on VPN is on, connections without VPN are blocked ✓
Now: Always-on VPN is on, but connections without VPN are not blocked

Opens a test site in your browser. The browser goes through the VPN like other apps; Hydra itself is excluded from the tunnel, so an in-app test would always show a “leak”. If the list shows your internet provider\'s DNS servers, DNS is leaking.
Connect the VPN first, otherwise the test shows your real connection.
Save the current DNS, geo routing, MTU, TLS fragmentation, IPv6 and split tunneling as a profile (“Home”, “Travel”) and switch in one tap.
+ Save current settings as a profile
Hydra checks the latest release on GitHub. The app does not download or install anything by itself: it opens the release page.
Once a day on app start. The request goes to api.github.com directly, not through the VPN.
